newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed Martin sales up 31 percent in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed Martin sales up 31 percent in Q1.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp said Tuesday that first quarter sales jumped 31 percent from a year earlier to $6.7 billion as it continued to win new business at an unprecedented rate.
The company also said it had a double-digit increase in earnings per share, to $1.34 from $1.22, improved operating profit margins, and strong cash flow.
"Our growth in new orders over the past 15 months has positioned us for solid top-line growth in 1997 and beyond," Vance Coffman, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement.
"We intend to continue to drive out costs to further improve our profitability," Coffman added.
The company said its backlog totaled $49.6 billion at the end of the first quarter, up from $42.6 billion a year ago.
It said most of its earnings and sales increases were due to the strategic combination with Loral's defense and electronics and systems integration business, which was completed in April 1996.
Lockheed said it keeps winning new business at an unprecedented rate, which it attributes to its consolidation activities with resulting cost savings and efficiences.
